narration.text: A household's recurring charges are audited: a second streaming account on the bank, a trial that became a charge, an add-on raised without notice and an unused storage plan cancelled, two refunded, while a son's and a partner's weekly use, a service used this week, a one-time purchase and a plan renewed after its reminder are left alone. This is a chore for a dental office manager in San Diego, California, who pays for streaming, a fitness app and cloud storage from a card and a bank account, with a son and a partner who use some of it. On the bench, she found 6 of 6 eligible items, worth 613 dollars and 50 cents of the 613 dollars and 50 cents there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 8 traps, and she walked past 8. She took 1 minute. By hand, the same chore takes 2 hours, so she was about 86 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
